def: n. a football play is changed orally after both teams have assumed their positions at the line of scrimmage
a. heard or perceptible by the ear

tr: n. 保險絲, 導火線
def: n. an electrical device that can interrupt the flow of electrical current when it is overloaded
n. any igniter that is used to initiate the burning of a propellant
v. become plastic or fluid or liquefied from heat

ex.en: The electrician replaced the fuse, and the lights came on.
ex.zh: 電工換了保險絲，燈就亮了。

ex.en: Modern design often fuses traditional craftsmanship with digital technology to create more sustainable consumer products.
ex.zh: 現代設計常將傳統工藝與數字技術融合，以創造更可持續的消費品。

col: blow a fuse｜燒斷保險絲；大發雷霆
words.tip: 作動詞指融合；blow a fuse也可比喻大發雷霆。

tr: vt. 製造, 建造, 裝配, 偽造
def: v. make up something artificial or untrue
To invent false information in order to deceive
To make a product or structure from separate materials

ex.en: He fabricated an excuse for missing the family dinner.
ex.zh: 他編了個藉口，解釋自己為什麼沒來參加家庭聚餐。

ex.en: Researchers who fabricate evidence undermine public trust in science and may influence important policy decisions.
ex.zh: 捏造證據的研究人員會損害公眾對科學的信任，並可能影響重要的政策決策。

words.tip: 既可指捏造信息，也可指工業製造，須看賓語。

tr: n. 膚色, 情況, 局面
[醫] 體質; 面色, 面容
def: n. the coloring of a person's face
n. a combination that results from coupling or interlinking
n. a point of view or general attitude or inclination

tr: n. 扳鉗, 扳手, 扭傷, 歪曲, 痛苦
vt. 猛扭, 扭傷, 曲解, 折磨
def: n. a sharp strain on muscles or ligaments
n. a hand tool that is used to hold or twist a nut or bolt
v. twist or pull violently or suddenly, especially so as to remove (something) from that to which it is attached or from where it originates

ex.en: She tightened the loose bolt with a wrench.
ex.zh: 她用扳手擰緊了鬆動的螺栓。

ex.en: Leaving a close community can be a real wrench for students who move abroad for university.
ex.zh: 對赴海外上大學的學生來說，離開關係緊密的社區可能十分難捨。

col: wrench something open｜猛力拉開某物
a real wrench｜難以割捨的痛苦
words.tip: 扳手在英式英語中常叫spanner；wrench也可作動詞。

tr: n. 佝僂, 屈從, 彎腰
vi. 彎下, 屈從, 彎腰, 墮落
vt. 使屈從, 使彎曲
def: n. an inclination of the top half of the body forward and downward
n. small porch or set of steps at the front entrance of a house
v. descend swiftly, as if on prey

ex.en: She stooped to pick up the fallen orange.
ex.zh: 她彎腰撿起掉落的橙子。

ex.en: Companies should not stoop to misleading advertising merely to increase sales in an increasingly competitive market.
ex.zh: 企業不應僅為在競爭日益激烈的市場中提高銷量，就不擇手段地發佈誤導性廣告。

col: stoop to pick something up｜彎腰撿東西
walk with a stoop｜佝僂著走路
words.tip: stoop to doing表示不惜做卑劣之事，to為介詞。

tr: n. 融解, 融化, 解凍時期
vt. 使融解, 使緩和
def: n. the process whereby heat changes something from a solid to a liquid
n. warm weather following a freeze; snow and ice melt
n. a relaxation or slackening of tensions or reserve; becoming less hostile

tr: a. 難的, 艱苦的, 堅硬的, 勇敢的
adv. 努力地, 辛苦地, 堅硬地
def: n. United States slapstick comedian who played the pompous and overbearing member of the Laurel and Hardy duo who made many films (1892-1957)
n. English novelist and poet (1840-1928)
s. having rugged physical strength; inured to fatigue or hardships

tr: [法] 林地, 林學, 林業
def: n. the science of planting and caring for forests and the management of growing timber

tr: a. 奢侈的, 揮霍無度的, 浪費的
def: s. recklessly wasteful
Spending or costing much more money than necessary.
Going beyond what is reasonable or believable.

ex.en: Buying another silk coat seemed extravagant on her budget.
ex.zh: 以她的預算來說，再買一件絲綢外套顯得太奢侈了。

ex.en: Extravagant spending on international events can divert public funds from essential healthcare and education services.
ex.zh: 在國際活動上過度花費可能擠佔基本醫療和教育服務所需的公共資金。

words.tip: 既可指花錢無度，也可指言辭或要求過分。

tr: vt. 質問, 訊問, 審問
def: v. transmit (a signal) for setting off an appropriate response, as in telecommunication
v. pose a series of questions to

tr: [機] 摘下, 分離, 卸下
def: v. cause to become detached or separated; take off
v. separate (a small unit) from a larger, especially for a special assignment
v. come to be detached

ex.en: You can detach the hood when the rain stops.
ex.zh: 雨停後，你可以把帽兜拆下來。

ex.en: Researchers must detach themselves from personal preferences when evaluating evidence to ensure that their conclusions remain reliable.
ex.zh: 研究人員評估證據時必須擺脫個人偏好的影響，以確保結論可靠。

col: detach yourself from｜使自己超脫於
words.tip: 常用 detach A from B；detachable 指可拆卸的。

def: n. drink made by steeping and boiling and fermenting rather than distilling
v. prepare by brewing
v. sit or let sit in boiling water so as to extract the flavor

tr: a. 不好不壞的, 通常, 平凡的
def: s. moderate to inferior in quality
s. poor to middling in quality

tr: a. 稀疏的, 稀稀落落的, 稀薄的
def: s. not dense

tr: n. 日元(日本貨幣單位), 渴望, 嗜好
def: n. the basic unit of money in Japan; equal to 100 sen

n. a reference work (often in several volumes) containing articles on various topics (often arranged in alphabetical order) dealing with the entire range of human knowledge or with some particular specialty
A book or website explaining many subjects or one field.

ex.en: I found a fascinating dinosaur picture in this encyclopedia.
ex.zh: 我在這本百科全書裡找到了一幅很有趣的恐龍圖片。

ex.en: An online encyclopedia offers convenient background information, but students should verify important claims using reliable academic sources.
ex.zh: 在線百科全書便於查詢背景信息，但學生應使用可靠的學術來源核實重要論斷。

col: consult an encyclopedia｜查閱百科全書
words.tip: 英式英語也常拼作encyclopaedia。

tr: n. 懊悔, 良心不安, 自責, 同情
[法] 悔恨, 自責, 懊悔
def: n a feeling of deep regret (usually for some misdeed)
s being ahead of time or need
r ahead of time; in anticipation

tr: n. 卷軸, 畫卷, 名冊, 條幅, 滾動
def: n. a document that can be rolled up (as for storage)
v. move through text or graphics in order to display parts that do not fit on the screen

tr: n. 行軍床, 小屋, (家畜等的)棚, (家畜等的)欄
def: n. a small bed that folds up for storage or transport

tr: a. 沉悶的, 冗長乏味的
def: s so lacking in interest as to cause mental weariness
s using or containing too many words
boring because it continues too long or involves repeated actions

ex.en: Sorting all these old receipts is a tedious job.
ex.zh: 整理這些舊收據是一件單調乏味的差事。

ex.en: Automation can free employees from tedious tasks, allowing them to focus on more creative and rewarding work.
ex.zh: 自動化可以讓員工擺脫單調的任務，專注於更有創意和成就感的工作。

words.tip: 常形容因耗時長或反覆重複而乏味的任務。

tr: n. 打油詩文, 詼諧的模仿詩文, 拙劣的模仿
vt. 拙劣模仿, 作模仿詩文
def: n. a composition that imitates or misrepresents somebody's style, usually in a humorous way
n. humorous or satirical mimicry
v. make a spoof of or make fun of

tr: vt. 使中立, 使成中立地帶, 使中和, 抵銷
vi. 中立化, 變無效, 中和
def: v. make politically neutral and thus inoffensive
v. make ineffective by counterbalancing the effect of
v. get rid of (someone who may be a threat) by killing

ex.en: This spray helps neutralize unpleasant smells in the kitchen.
ex.zh: 這種噴霧有助於消除廚房裡的異味。

ex.en: Farmers sometimes add lime to acidic soil to neutralize excess acidity and improve conditions for crop growth.
ex.zh: 農民有時會向酸性土壤中施加石灰，中和過多的酸性，改善作物生長條件。

words.tip: 英式也拼neutralise；強調抵消作用，不一定移除物體。

tr: a. 疾馳的, 短暫的, 飛逝的
def: s. lasting for a markedly brief time

tr: n. 偏執狂, 多疑症
def: n. a psychological disorder characterized by delusions of persecution or grandeur
An unfounded belief that others intend to harm you.

ex.en: Her growing paranoia made ordinary conversations feel threatening.
ex.zh: 她日益加重的被害妄想讓普通交談也顯得充滿威脅。

ex.en: Mental health services should offer compassionate support to people experiencing paranoia rather than reinforcing harmful stereotypes.
ex.zh: 心理健康服務應向受偏執困擾的人提供關懷與支持，而不是強化有害的刻板印象。

col: feelings of paranoia｜受迫害的疑懼感
paranoia about surveillance｜對被監視的過度疑懼
words.tip: 通常不可數；指心理狀態，不指患有此症的人。

tr: n. 爬行動物, 爬蟲, 卑鄙的人
a. 爬行的, 爬蟲類的, 卑鄙的
def: n. any cold-blooded vertebrate of the class Reptilia including tortoises, turtles, snakes, lizards, alligators, crocodiles, and extinct forms
a cold-blooded animal with scaly skin, such as a snake

ex.en: The reptile lay perfectly still on a warm rock.
ex.zh: 那隻爬行動物一動不動地趴在一塊溫熱的岩石上。

ex.en: Many reptile species depend on external heat sources to regulate their body temperature throughout the day.
ex.zh: 許多爬行動物物種依靠外部熱源來調節全天的體溫。

col: reptile enclosure｜爬行動物飼養圍欄
words.tip: 蛇、蜥蜴、龜屬爬行動物；青蛙不屬此類。

tr: a. 宏偉的, 莊嚴的
def: s. majestic in manner or bearing; superior to mundane matters

tr: vt. 嘉獎, 委託給, 推薦
def: v. express approval of
v. present as worthy of regard, kindness, or confidence
v. give to in charge

ex.en: The coach commended Lina for helping her teammates.
ex.zh: 教練表揚莉娜幫助了隊友。

ex.en: Inspectors commended the school for providing additional support to students with different learning needs.
ex.zh: 督察人員讚揚該校為有不同學習需求的學生提供額外支持。

col: commend someone for something｜因某事表揚某人
commend something to someone｜向某人推薦某物
words.tip: commend是稱讚；command是命令，注意拼寫。

tr: n. 夜總會, 迪斯科, 的士高
def: n. popular dance music (especially in the late 1970s); melodic with a regular bass beat; intended mainly for dancing at discotheques
n. a public dance hall for dancing to recorded popular music
v. dance to disco music

tr: n. 彈回, 有彈力, 恢復力
[化] 回彈; 彈性; 彈回性; 回能; 彈能
def: n. the physical property of a material that can return to its original shape or position after deformation that does not exceed its elastic limit
n. an occurrence of rebounding or springing back
The ability to recover or adapt after difficulties

ex.en: Her resilience helped her rebuild after the flood.
ex.zh: 她憑藉堅韌的復原力在洪災後重建了生活。

ex.en: Strong community networks can increase resilience by providing practical and emotional support during economic crises.
ex.zh: 緊密的社區網絡能在經濟危機期間提供實際幫助和情感支持，從而增強抗逆力。

col: show remarkable resilience｜展現非凡的復原力
words.tip: 通常不可數，強調受挫後的恢復與適應能力。

tr: n. 閃耀, 火花, 活力, 發泡
def: n. merriment expressed by a brightness or gleam or animation of countenance
v. reflect brightly
v. be lively or brilliant or exhibit virtuosity

ex.en: The tiny crystals sparkle whenever sunlight enters the room.
ex.zh: 每當陽光照進房間，那些小水晶就閃閃發亮。

ex.en: Although the river sparkles in the sunlight, regular testing is necessary to assess its water quality.
ex.zh: 儘管河水在陽光下波光粼粼，仍需定期檢測以評估水質。

col: sparkle in the sunlight｜在陽光下閃耀
words.tip: sparkle強調點點閃光；shine泛指發光。

def: a. suitable for use as food
Safe or suitable to eat.

ex.en: These edible flowers make the salad look especially colourful.
ex.zh: 這些可食用的花讓沙拉顯得格外繽紛。

ex.en: Redistributing edible food that shops would otherwise discard could reduce waste and support families on low incomes.
ex.zh: 將商店原本會丟棄的可食用食物重新分配，可以減少浪費並幫助低收入家庭。

words.tip: edible表示能吃，不表示美味；勿憑外觀判斷野生植物。

def: n. a small book usually having a paper cover
a small, thin book, usually containing practical information

ex.en: The nurse gave me a booklet about healthy eating.
ex.zh: 護士給了我一本介紹健康飲食的小冊子。

ex.en: An illustrated booklet can make essential health advice more accessible to patients with limited reading skills.
ex.zh: 一本配有插圖的小冊子可以讓閱讀能力有限的患者更容易理解重要的健康建議。

col: a booklet on｜關於……的小冊子
words.tip: -let常表示小；booklet是薄薄的小冊子。

def: n. a glass filled to the brim (especially as a toast)
n. a mechanical device consisting of bars at either end of a vehicle to absorb shock and prevent serious damage

tr: vt. 花費, 消耗, 用光
def: v use up, consume fully
v pay out

tr: n. 古怪的人, 漂泊無定的人
a. 不穩定的, 奇怪的
def: s. liable to sudden unpredictable change
s. having no fixed course
s. likely to perform unpredictably; sometimes it would start and sometimes it wouldn't"

tr: a. 互惠的, 相互的, 相等的, 倒數的, 彼此相反的
n. 倒數, 互相起作用的事物
def: n. something (a term or expression or concept) that has a reciprocal relation to something else
a. concerning each of two or more persons or things; especially given or done in return
s. of or relating to the multiplicative inverse of a quantity or function

tr: a. 喜不自禁的, 歡鬧的, 引人發笑的
def: s. marked by or causing boisterous merriment or convulsive laughter
extremely funny and likely to make people laugh

ex.en: Her hilarious story made everyone laugh throughout dinner.
ex.zh: 她那個特別好笑的故事讓大家吃飯時笑個不停。

ex.en: Although hilarious advertisements can attract attention, humour does not always help consumers remember the product being promoted.
ex.zh: 雖然令人捧腹的廣告能夠吸引注意，但幽默並不總能幫助消費者記住所推銷的產品。

words.tip: 強調“極其好笑”，不只是熱鬧或開心。

def: v force to go away; used both with concrete and metaphoric meanings
v to cause to separate and go in different directions
v. leave one's country of residence for a new one
To leave your country to live permanently in another

ex.en: Her grandparents emigrated to Canada when they were young.
ex.zh: 她的祖父母年輕時移居到了加拿大。

ex.en: Skilled workers may emigrate when their home countries offer limited opportunities for professional development.
ex.zh: 當本國提供的職業發展機會有限時，技術人才可能會移居國外。

words.tip: emigrate強調遷出，immigrate強調遷入；搭配from或to。

def: n. payment made to a person in a position of trust to corrupt his judgment
v. make illegal payments to in exchange for favors or influence
Offer rewards to make someone act dishonestly in your favour.

ex.en: The driver tried to bribe the officer with cash.
ex.zh: 那名司機試圖用現金賄賂警察。

ex.en: Strict penalties for companies that bribe public officials can help restore trust in government institutions.
ex.zh: 嚴懲向公職人員行賄的公司，有助於恢復公眾對政府機構的信任。

col: bribe someone into doing something｜賄賂某人做某事
words.tip: bribe的賓語是受賄者；bribery指行賄受賄行為。

tr: n. 高潮, 極點, 層進法
v. (使)達到頂點, (使)達到高潮
def: n. the highest point of anything conceived of as growing or developing or unfolding
n. the decisive moment in a novel or play
n. the most severe stage of a disease

ex.en: The concert reached its climax when the whole choir joined.
ex.zh: 整個合唱團加入演唱時，音樂會達到了高潮。

ex.en: The film reaches its climax when the community unites to protect the forest from destruction.
ex.zh: 當社區居民團結起來保護森林免遭破壞時，影片達到了高潮。

col: a dramatic climax｜扣人心絃的高潮
words.tip: climactic指高潮的；別與climatic（氣候的）混淆。

tr: vt. 阻隔, 妨礙, 阻塞, 遮沒
def: v. hinder or prevent the progress or accomplishment of
v. block passage through
v. shut out from view or get in the way so as to hide from sight

tr: vt. 一般化, 概括, 推廣
vi. 形成概念, 籠統講
def: v. draw from specific cases for more general cases
v. speak or write in generalities
v. become systemic and spread throughout the body
n. the usage or vocabulary that is characteristic of a specific group of people
A language variety used in a particular region or community.

ex.en: My grandmother speaks a dialect I sometimes struggle to understand.
ex.zh: 我奶奶說一種我有時聽不太懂的方言。

ex.en: Schools can help preserve local dialects while teaching students the standard language needed for wider communication.
ex.zh: 學校可以在教授學生廣泛交流所需的標準語的同時，幫助保護當地方言。

words.tip: dialect涉及詞彙和語法，accent主要指口音。

tr: n. 登記, 註冊, 入伍, 入學, 入會, 註冊人數, 入學人數
def: n the act of enrolling

tr: [法] 不可靠的, 靠不住的
def: a. not worthy of reliance or trust
s. lacking a sense of responsibility

tr: vi. 減少, 縮小, 衰落
def: v. become smaller or lose substance
Gradually become smaller in amount, size, or number.

ex.en: Our savings dwindled while we searched for new jobs.
ex.zh: 我們找新工作期間，積蓄逐漸減少了。

ex.en: As freshwater supplies dwindle, governments must invest in efficient irrigation and encourage households to reduce unnecessary consumption.
ex.zh: 隨著淡水供應逐漸減少，政府必須投資高效灌溉，並鼓勵家庭減少不必要的用水。

words.tip: 不及物動詞，強調逐漸減少，不能直接接賓語。

tr: vi. 欣喜, 高興, 慶祝
def: v. feel happiness or joy
Feel or show great happiness about something.

ex.en: We rejoiced when our missing cat finally came home.
ex.zh: 失蹤的貓終於回家了，我們欣喜不已。

ex.en: Residents rejoiced at the reopening of their local library, which provides valuable educational resources.
ex.zh: 當地居民為圖書館重新開放而歡欣鼓舞，因為它提供了寶貴的教育資源。

col: rejoice at the news｜為消息感到欣喜
rejoice in someone's success｜為某人的成功歡喜
words.tip: 較正式；常用rejoice at/in或接that從句。

def: n. a propelling force
n. the act of propelling
The force or process that moves something forward

ex.en: This small boat relies on electric propulsion to move quietly.
ex.zh: 這艘小船靠電力推進，行駛時很安靜。

ex.en: Advances in electric propulsion could reduce both noise pollution and fuel consumption in coastal shipping.
ex.zh: 電力推進技術的進步有望減少沿海航運的噪聲汙染和燃料消耗。

words.tip: 通常為不可數名詞，常用於船舶、飛機和航天器。

tr: a. 提供消息的, 見聞廣博的
def: a. providing or conveying information

tr: a. 名義上的, 名字的, 有名無實的, 稍許的
def: a. relating to or constituting or bearing or giving a name
s. insignificantly small; a matter of form only (`tokenish' is informal)
a. pertaining to a noun or to a word group that functions as a noun

tr: n. 漏斗, 漏斗狀的東西, 煙囪
def: n. a conical shape with a wider and a narrower opening at the two ends
n. a conically shaped utensil having a narrow tube at the small end; used to channel the flow of substances into a container with a small mouth
n. (nautical) smokestack consisting of a shaft for ventilation or the passage of smoke (especially the smokestack of a ship)

ex.en: Use a funnel to pour oil into the bottle.
ex.zh: 用漏斗把油倒進瓶子裡。

ex.en: Well-designed drainage systems funnel rainwater into storage tanks, reducing the risk of urban flooding.
ex.zh: 設計合理的排水系統將雨水引入儲水罐，降低城市內澇風險。

words.tip: 作動詞常用funnel A into B，表示將A引入B。

tr: a. 狂熱的, 盲信的
def: n. a person motivated by irrational enthusiasm (as for a cause)
s. marked by excessive enthusiasm for and intense devotion to a cause or idea
Someone who is extremely enthusiastic about an activity or interest.

ex.en: My cousin is a fitness fanatic who exercises daily.
ex.zh: 我表親是個健身迷，每天都鍛鍊。

ex.en: A political fanatic may reject reasonable debate, making it harder for communities to resolve disagreements peacefully.
ex.zh: 政治狂熱者可能拒絕理性辯論，使社會群體更難和平解決分歧。

words.tip: 愛好語境可輕鬆使用；信仰語境常含貶義。

tr: adv. 極端地, 極度地, 非常
def: r to an extreme degree
To a very great degree.

ex.en: The little bakery was exceedingly busy on Saturday morning.
ex.zh: 週六早上，那家小麵包店忙得不可開交。

ex.en: Providing reliable public transport in sparsely populated areas can be exceedingly expensive for local authorities.
ex.zh: 對於地方政府而言，在人口稀少的地區提供可靠的公共交通可能極其昂貴。

words.tip: 比 very 更正式，常修飾形容詞或副詞。

tr: a. 馴服的, 柔順的, 被開墾的, 順從的, 乏味的, 平淡的
vt. 馴養, 馴服, 制服, 失去鋒芒
def: v. correct by punishment or discipline
s. flat and uninspiring
a. very restrained or quiet

ex.en: The tame rabbit ate directly from my hand.
ex.zh: 那隻溫順的兔子直接吃我手裡的食物。

ex.en: Even tame animals require careful handling, especially when young children are learning to interact with them.
ex.zh: 即使是馴服的動物也需要謹慎對待，尤其是在幼兒學習與它們互動時。

words.tip: tame指不怕人或被馴服，不等於天生無害。

tr: n. 衛生保健, 衛生學, 保健法
def: n. a condition promoting sanitary practices
n. the science concerned with the prevention of illness and maintenance of health
s (sometimes followed by `to') causing harm or injury

tr: n. 評價, 估價, 價值判斷
[經] 估價, 計價, 評價
def: n. assessed price

tr: n. 震搖, 搖動, 顛簸
vi. 顛簸而行, 震搖
vt. 使顛簸, 使慌張, 猛擊
def: n. a sudden jarring impact
v. move or cause to move with a sudden jerky motion
v. disturb (someone's) composure

tr: a. 熱心的, 激動的, 燃燒般的
def: s. characterized by intense emotion
s. characterized by strong enthusiasm
s. glowing or shining like fire

tr: a. 公正的, 正義的, 正直的
[法] 正直的, 正當的, 正義的
def: a. characterized by or proceeding from accepted standards of morality or justice
s. morally justified
morally right or acting according to strong moral principles

ex.en: She believed returning the wallet was the righteous choice.
ex.zh: 她認為歸還錢包才是正直的選擇。

ex.en: Righteous anger at social injustice can encourage citizens to demand meaningful changes in public policy.
ex.zh: 對社會不公的義憤可以促使公民要求公共政策作出實質性改變。

words.tip: 語氣較莊重；self-righteous指自以為正直。

tr: a. 暫時的, 暫定的, 臨時的
def: s under terms not final or fully worked out or agreed upon

tr: vt. 付還, 償還借款
def: n. money returned to a payer
n. the act of returning money received previously
v. pay back

ex.en: The shop gave me a refund for the broken kettle.
ex.zh: 商店把壞水壺的貨款退給了我。

ex.en: Airlines should offer passengers a full refund when flights are cancelled without reasonable alternatives.
ex.zh: 航班取消且沒有合理的替代方案時，航空公司應向乘客提供全額退款。

words.tip: 名詞重音在前；動詞讀/rɪˈfʌnd/，重音在後。

tr: vt. 歸因於, 歸咎於
def: v attribute or credit to
To consider something to be caused by a particular factor
To assign a quality, work, or statement to someone

ex.en: I ascribe my better sleep to regular evening walks.
ex.zh: 我認為睡眠改善得益於每晚定時散步。

ex.en: Researchers should not ascribe differences in academic performance solely to individual effort without considering social circumstances.
ex.zh: 研究人員不應在未考慮社會環境的情況下，將學業表現的差異完全歸因於個人努力。

col: ascribe success to｜將成功歸因於
ascribe a work to｜認定作品出自
words.tip: 固定結構ascribe A to B：把A歸因於B。

tr: n. 覺醒, 奮起, 乾杯
vt. 喚醒, 鼓舞, 激動, 使振奮, 驚起
def: v become active
v force or drive out
v cause to be agitated, excited, or roused

ex.en: The smell of breakfast finally roused him from sleep.
ex.zh: 早餐的香味終於把他從睡夢中喚醒了。

ex.en: Powerful images of polluted rivers can rouse public concern and encourage stronger support for environmental protection.
ex.zh: 受汙染河流的震撼畫面能激起公眾關注，促使人們更大力支持環境保護。

col: rouse someone from sleep｜把某人從睡夢中喚醒
rouse someone to action｜激勵某人行動
words.tip: rouse sb from sleep表喚醒；rouse interest表激起。

tr: vt. 使喘不過氣, 使窒息, 悶熄, 忍住, 抑制, 覆蓋
n. 濃煙, 窒息狀態, 雜亂無章
def: n. a stifling cloud of smoke
v. envelop completely
v. deprive of oxygen and prevent from breathing

tr: vt. 逐放, 放逐, 噴射
def: v. put out or expel from a place
v. leave an aircraft rapidly, using an ejection seat or capsule
v. specify as a condition or requirement in a contract or agreement; make an express demand or provision in an agreement
v. give a guarantee or promise of
v. make an oral contract or agreement in the verbal form of question and answer that is necessary to give it legal force

ex.en: The rental rules stipulate that pets must stay downstairs.
ex.zh: 租賃規定明確要求寵物必須待在樓下。

ex.en: Employment contracts should stipulate working hours clearly to prevent disputes between employers and their staff.
ex.zh: 勞動合同應明確規定工作時間，以防止僱主與員工發生爭議。

col: stipulate a deadline｜規定截止日期
words.tip: 正式用詞，常用於合同；可接名詞或that從句。

tr: a. 過期的, 未兌的, 遲到的, 早就成熟的
def: s past due; not paid at the scheduled time
Not paid, returned, or completed by the expected time.
Needed or deserved much earlier than now.

ex.en: I found an overdue library book under my bed.
ex.zh: 我在床底下發現了一本逾期未還的圖書館藏書。

ex.en: Investment in rural public transport is long overdue, as many residents still lack reliable services.
ex.zh: 農村公共交通早就該得到投資，因為許多居民至今仍缺乏可靠的交通服務。

col: an overdue library book｜逾期未還的圖書館書籍
words.tip: long overdue強調“早就該有或該做”，不只是遲到。

tr: a. 有生殖力的, 多產的, 豐富的
[醫] 多育的, 多產的, 繁殖的
def: s. bearing in abundance especially offspring
Producing many works, results or achievements.
Producing many young, flowers, fruits or seeds.

ex.en: My aunt is a prolific painter with two studios.
ex.zh: 我姑姑是位多產的畫家，擁有兩間畫室。

ex.en: Prolific researchers can contribute substantially to scientific progress, but publication quantity should not outweigh quality.
ex.zh: 成果豐碩的研究者能大力推動科學進步，但發表數量不應比質量更受重視。

col: a prolific breeder｜繁殖力強的動物
words.tip: 強調產出多，不等於作品質量一定高。

tr: vt. 檢查, 審查, 刪改
def: n. someone who censures or condemns
n. a person who is authorized to read publications or correspondence or to watch theatrical performances and suppress in whole or in part anything considered obscene or politically unacceptable
v. subject to political, religious, or moral censorship

tr: vt. 分解檢查, 翻修, 精細檢查, 徹底革新
n. 分解檢查, 精細檢查, 大檢修
def: n. periodic maintenance on a car or machine
v. make repairs, renovations, revisions or adjustments to

tr: a. 有益於...的, 有助於...的, 助長的
def: s. tending to bring about; being partly responsible for

tr: vt. 使失去能力, 使殘廢, (律)使無資格
[計] 使無效, 禁止, 關閉
def: v. make unable to perform a certain action
v. injure permanently
to prevent a device or feature from working

ex.en: I disabled notifications so my phone stayed quiet during dinner.
ex.zh: 我關閉了通知，讓手機在吃晚飯時保持安靜。

ex.en: Users should be able to disable location tracking without losing access to essential digital services.
ex.zh: 用戶應當能夠禁用位置追蹤，而不失去使用基本數字服務的權限。

col: disable location tracking｜禁用位置追蹤
words.tip: 技術語境常指“禁用”，不表示刪除或損壞。

tr: a. 可笑的, 滑稽的, 荒唐的
def: s broadly or extravagantly humorous; resembling farce
s incongruous; inviting ridicule

tr: n. 群, 人群, 群集, 眾多
vt. 在...群集, 使擁塞
def: v. press tightly together or cram
a large crowd of people gathered closely together
to gather somewhere in large numbers

ex.en: We pushed through the throng to reach the exit.
ex.zh: 我們擠過人群，來到出口。

ex.en: Throngs of visitors can place considerable pressure on historic sites during the peak tourist season.
ex.zh: 在旅遊旺季，大批遊客可能給歷史遺址帶來相當大的壓力。

col: a throng of people｜一大群人
words.tip: 偏書面；a throng of後接複數名詞。

tr: n. 最適條件, 最佳效果
a. 最優的, 最適宜的
def: n. most favorable conditions or greatest degree or amount possible under given circumstances
s. most desirable possible under a restriction expressed or implied
best suited to achieving a particular result

ex.en: This sunny windowsill provides optimum conditions for my herbs.
ex.zh: 這個陽光充足的窗臺為我種的香草提供了最適宜的條件。

ex.en: Maintaining the optimum classroom temperature can help students concentrate and reduce the energy required for heating.
ex.zh: 保持最適宜的教室溫度有助於學生集中注意力，並減少供暖能耗。

words.tip: 強調最適合目標，並非越多越好；通常不用most修飾。

tr: n. 神智健全, 頭腦清楚, 通情達理
def: n. normal or sound powers of mind

tr: n. 復活, 復興, 文藝復興
def: n. the period of European history at the close of the Middle Ages and the rise of the modern world; a cultural rebirth from the 14th through the middle of the 17th centuries
a period of renewed interest, activity, or success
the European period of renewed classical learning and artistic development

ex.en: Our local theatre is enjoying a renaissance this summer.
ex.zh: 今年夏天，我們當地的劇院再度煥發生機。

ex.en: Investment in public galleries could encourage a cultural renaissance in cities affected by industrial decline.
ex.zh: 投資公共美術館可能推動受工業衰退影響的城市實現文化復興。

words.tip: 指歷史上的文藝復興時通常大寫並加the。

tr: a. 精明的, 銳利的, 劇烈的, 機靈的, 厲害的
def: s marked by practical hardheaded intelligence
s used of persons
good at judging situations and making decisions that bring advantages

ex.en: That shrewd purchase saved us money on heating.
ex.zh: 那次明智的購買為我們節省了取暖費用。

ex.en: Shrewd investment in renewable energy can help governments reduce future costs while improving national energy security.
ex.zh: 對可再生能源進行精明投資，可以幫助政府降低未來成本，同時提升國家能源安全。

col: a shrewd investor｜精明的投資者
words.tip: 強調判斷精明、善於謀利，不等於單純聰明。

tr: a. 裝滿的, 負載的, 苦惱的
def: s. filled with a great quantity
s. burdened psychologically or mentally
Carrying or holding a large amount of something.

ex.en: She arrived at the picnic laden with bags of food.
ex.zh: 她帶著大包小包的食物來到野餐地點。

ex.en: Trucks laden with construction materials contribute to congestion and increase road maintenance costs in rapidly expanding cities.
ex.zh: 在迅速擴張的城市中，滿載建築材料的卡車加劇了擁堵，並增加了道路維護成本。

words.tip: 常用laden with；也可構成sugar-laden等複合形容詞。

tr: n. 長官, 法官, 推事
[法] 司法行政官, 治安法官, 地方法官
def: n. a lay judge or civil authority who administers the law (especially one who conducts a court dealing with minor offenses)

tr: n. 地方, 所在, 位置
[法] 位置, 場所, 地區
def: n a surrounding or nearby region
n a state of peace agreed to between opponents so they can discuss peace terms
An agreement to stop fighting or arguing for a time

ex.en: After arguing all morning, the neighbours called a truce.
ex.zh: 爭吵了一上午後，鄰居們暫時休戰了。

ex.en: A temporary truce can allow aid workers to deliver essential supplies to communities affected by conflict.
ex.zh: 臨時停戰可以讓援助人員向受衝突影響的社區運送必需物資。

col: agree to a truce｜同意停戰
break a truce｜破壞休戰協議
words.tip: 通常指暫時停止衝突，不等於永久和平。

tr: a. 一絲不苟的, 精確的, 過細的
def: s. marked by precise accordance with details
s. marked by extreme care in treatment of details
Extremely careful and attentive to every small detail.

ex.en: He made meticulous notes while repairing the old clock.
ex.zh: 他修理舊鐘時做了細緻的記錄。

ex.en: Meticulous planning is essential when researchers conduct experiments involving complex equipment and sensitive environmental measurements.
ex.zh: 研究人員開展涉及複雜設備和精密環境測量的實驗時，周密規劃至關重要。

col: meticulous attention to detail｜對細節的一絲不苟
words.tip: 通常是褒義，強調認真關注每個細節。

tr: a. 顯赫的, 傑出的, 有名的
def: s. standing above others in quality or position
s. of imposing height; especially standing out above others
Famous and respected for achievements in a particular field.

ex.en: An eminent surgeon visited our local hospital yesterday.
ex.zh: 一位傑出的外科醫生昨天來訪了我們當地的醫院。

ex.en: Universities often invite eminent researchers to share their findings and inspire students to pursue academic careers.
ex.zh: 大學常邀請傑出的研究人員分享研究成果，激勵學生從事學術工作。

words.tip: eminent指傑出；imminent指即將發生。

tr: n. 消遣, 娛樂, 遊戲
def: n. a diversion that occupies one's time and thoughts (usually pleasantly)
An activity you enjoy doing in your free time.

ex.en: Gardening became her favourite pastime after she retired.
ex.zh: 退休後，園藝成了她最喜歡的消遣。

ex.en: Outdoor pastimes can improve mental health while encouraging people to spend less time using electronic devices.
ex.zh: 戶外休閒活動可以改善心理健康，同時鼓勵人們減少使用電子設備的時間。

words.tip: 指閒暇活動；注意拼寫只有一個s。

tr: vt. 使浸水, 使陷入, 淹沒
def: v. sink below the surface; go under or as if under water
v. cover completely or make imperceptible
v. put under water

ex.en: Submerge the dirty jar in warm water before washing it.
ex.zh: 清洗髒罐子前，先把它浸沒在溫水中。

ex.en: Rising sea levels could submerge low-lying coastal settlements, forcing residents to relocate and placing pressure on nearby cities.
ex.zh: 海平面上升可能淹沒地勢低窪的沿海聚居區，迫使居民遷移，並給附近城市帶來壓力。

words.tip: 可及物或不及物；強調進入水面或液麵以下。

tr: vt. 使滲透, 浸透, 使充滿, 使飽和
a. 浸透的, 飽和度高的, 深顏色的
n. 飽和化合物, 飽和脂肪酸
def: v. cause (a chemical compound, vapour, solution, magnetic material) to unite with the greatest possible amount of another substance

tr: n. 刺, 棘, 荊棘
def: n. a Germanic character of runic origin

tr: a. 小心的, 慎重的
def: a. marked by prudence or modesty and wise self-restraint
Careful not to reveal secrets or cause embarrassment.
Designed or chosen to avoid attracting attention.

ex.en: Please be discreet about the surprise party we're planning.
ex.zh: 請不要洩露我們正在籌備驚喜派對的事。

ex.en: Healthcare professionals must be discreet when discussing patients to protect their privacy and maintain public trust.
ex.zh: 醫護人員討論患者情況時必須謹慎，以保護患者隱私並維護公眾信任。

col: a discreet entrance｜不顯眼的入口
words.tip: 勿混discrete（分離的）；discreet強調謹慎低調。

tr: a. 同種的, 同質的, 齊性的
[醫] 同種的, 純一的, 同質的, 均勻的
def: a. all of the same or similar kind or nature
Consisting of parts or people that are all similar

ex.en: Stir the sauce until the mixture is completely homogeneous.
ex.zh: 攪拌醬汁，直到混合物完全均勻。

ex.en: Treating urban populations as homogeneous can lead planners to overlook important differences in residents' needs.
ex.zh: 將城市人口視為同質群體，可能導致規劃者忽視居民需求的重要差異。

words.tip: 強調組成部分相似或一致，反義詞為heterogeneous。

tr: vt. 逐退, 抵制, 使厭惡, 抗禦
vi. 使厭惡, 相互排斥
def: v. cause to move back by force or influence
v. be repellent to; cause aversion in
v. force or drive back

ex.en: This spray helps repel mosquitoes when we eat outside.
ex.zh: 我們在戶外吃飯時，這種噴霧有助於驅蚊。

ex.en: Modern outdoor clothing uses specially treated fabrics that repel water while allowing moisture to escape.
ex.zh: 現代戶外服裝採用經過特殊處理的面料，既能防水，又能排出溼氣。

words.tip: 過去式 repelled，動名詞 repelling，雙寫l。

tr: a. 殘忍的, 兇猛的, 可怕的
def: s. marked by extreme and violent energy
very fierce, violent, or aggressive
extremely strong or intense

ex.en: The ferocious dog growled from behind the locked gate.
ex.zh: 那隻兇猛的狗在鎖著的大門後低吼。

ex.en: Ferocious competition in the technology sector can encourage innovation but also threaten the survival of smaller firms.
ex.zh: 科技行業的激烈競爭能夠促進創新，但也可能威脅較小企業的生存。

col: a ferocious storm｜猛烈的暴風雨
words.tip: 既可形容動物兇猛，也可形容競爭或風暴猛烈。

tr: vt. 恢復原狀, 修復, 使康復
[法] 恢復, 使恢復心理健康, 修復
def: v. help to readapt, as to a former state of health or good repute
v. reinstall politically
v. restore to a state of good condition or operation

tr: [經] 司庫, 出納員, 收支員
def: n. a person responsible for receiving payments for goods and services (as in a shop or restaurant)
v. discard or do away with
v. discharge with dishonor, as in the army

ex.en: The cashier smiled and handed me my change.
ex.zh: 收銀員微笑著把零錢遞給我。

ex.en: Automated checkouts may reduce demand for cashiers, although many customers still prefer assistance from a person.
ex.zh: 自助結賬設備可能減少對收銀員的需求，但許多顧客仍更喜歡人工協助。

col: work as a cashier｜當收銀員
pay the cashier｜向收銀員付款
words.tip: cashier負責收款，accountant負責會計核算。

tr: n. 光彩, 假象, 註釋
vt. 使光彩, 掩蓋, 上光於, 註釋, 曲解
def: n. an explanation or definition of an obscure word in a text
v. give a shine or gloss to, usually by rubbing
v. provide interlinear explanations for words or phrases
s. subject to or caused by an earthquake or earth vibration

tr: a. 講話的, 適於說的, 講某種語言的
def: n. the utterance of intelligible speech
a. capable of or involving speech or speaking

tr: a. 更遠的, 此外的, 更多的
vt. 促進, 增進, 助長
adv. 更進一步地, 更遠地, 此外
def: s. more distant in especially degree
r. to or at a greater extent or degree or a more advanced stage (`further' is used more often than `farther' in this abstract sense)
r. in addition or furthermore; further, they should be here already"

ex.en: We walked further along the beach before stopping.
ex.zh: 我們沿著海灘又走了一段才停下。

ex.en: Further research is needed to understand how urban green spaces affect residents' mental health.
ex.zh: 還需要進一步研究，才能瞭解城市綠地如何影響居民的心理健康。

col: further your career｜促進職業發展
words.tip: further可指程度或距離；farther主要指距離。

tr: n. 旅程, 旅行指南, 遊記
a. 巡迴的, 旅程的
def: n an established line of travel or access
n a guidebook for travelers
n a proposed route of travel

tr: n. 少量食物, 細咬, 輕咬, 啃
v. 一點一點地咬, 細咬, 吹毛求疵
def: n. gentle biting
v. bite off very small pieces
v. bite gently

tr: a. 節儉的, 經濟的, 合算的
def: s. avoiding waste

tr: n. 湧出, 滔滔不絕地講話
v. 湧出, 迸出, 滔滔不絕的講話
def: n a sudden rapid flow (as of water)
n an unrestrained expression of emotion
v gush forth in a sudden stream or jet

ex.en: Water gushed from the broken pipe beneath the sink.
ex.zh: 水從水槽下方破裂的管道里噴湧而出。

ex.en: When ageing pipes burst, clean water can gush into streets, wasting resources and disrupting local transport.
ex.zh: 老化的管道爆裂時，清水會湧上街道，浪費資源並擾亂當地交通。

col: gush from a pipe｜從管道中噴出
gush about something｜對某事讚不絕口
a gush of water｜一股湧出的水
words.tip: 談論人時，gush about常暗示讚美過於熱情。

tr: n. 蔓延, 風行一時, 超過限度
vt. 蔓延, 蹂躪, 超過, 氾濫
vi. 氾濫, 超載限度
def: v. seize the position of and defeat
v. run beyond or past
To spread through or occupy a place in unwanted numbers.

ex.en: Weeds have overrun the garden since our neighbours moved away.
ex.zh: 鄰居搬走後，花園裡就長滿了雜草。

ex.en: Major infrastructure projects often overrun their budgets when planners underestimate material costs and construction delays.
ex.zh: 規劃者低估材料成本和施工延誤時，大型基礎設施項目往往會超支。

col: be overrun with weeds｜雜草叢生
words.tip: 變化為overran、overrun；名詞重音在首音節。

tr: n. 逐出, 開除, 驅逐, 排氣
def: n. the act of expelling or projecting or ejecting
The act of officially forcing someone to leave a place.
The process of forcing something out of a space or body.

ex.en: Repeated cheating led to his expulsion from the club.
ex.zh: 反覆作弊導致他被俱樂部開除。

ex.en: Schools should consider supportive interventions before expulsion, as exclusion can seriously damage a young person's educational prospects.
ex.zh: 學校在開除學生之前應考慮採取支持性干預措施，因為排斥可能嚴重損害年輕人的教育前景。

words.tip: 常用expulsion from；對應動詞為expel。

tr: vt. 尊敬, 尊重, 認為
def: n. the condition of being honored (esteemed or respected or well regarded)
Respect and admiration for someone.
To respect and admire someone highly.

ex.en: Her neighbours hold her in esteem for her kindness.
ex.zh: 鄰居們因她的善良而敬重她。

ex.en: Teachers who treat students fairly often earn the lasting esteem of their local communities.
ex.zh: 公平對待學生的教師往往能贏得當地社區長久的敬重。

col: hold someone in high esteem｜非常敬重某人
earn someone's esteem｜贏得某人的敬重
words.tip: 常用hold someone in high esteem表示非常敬重某人。

tr: vt. 設路障於, 阻礙
def: n. a barrier (usually thrown up hastily) to impede the advance of an enemy
v. render unsuitable for passage
v. prevent access to by barricading
v. cause to go crazy; cause to lose one's mind
v. drive up the wall; go on someone's nerves
v. make mad

ex.en: The constant buzzing of that broken fan maddens me.
ex.zh: 那臺壞風扇不停的嗡嗡聲讓我煩透了。

ex.en: Repeated delays and unclear explanations can madden commuters who depend on reliable public transport.
ex.zh: 反覆延誤和含糊的解釋會讓依賴可靠公共交通的通勤者極為惱火。

col: be maddened by delays｜因延誤而抓狂
words.tip: 通常是及物動詞，表示使某人惱怒到抓狂。

tr: [經] 扣除, 減去, 折扣
def: v make a subtraction
v retain and refrain from disbursing; of payments
v reason by deduction; establish by deduction

tr: a. 商定的, 協定的, 一致的
[法] 一致的, 協力的, 共同的
協同一致的；共同籌劃的
def: s. involving the joint activity of two or more
Planned and carried out together to achieve a shared goal.
Involving determined effort directed towards a particular goal.

ex.en: Our concerted efforts finally cleared the garden of rubbish.
ex.zh: 我們齊心協力，終於清除了花園裡的垃圾。

ex.en: Reducing urban air pollution requires concerted action from local authorities, transport providers, businesses and residents.
ex.zh: 減少城市空氣汙染需要地方政府、交通服務商、企業和居民採取協同行動。

col: concerted effort｜共同努力；全力投入
words.tip: 常修飾effort或action，強調協同或集中全力。

def: n. the sound of heavy treading or stomping
v. injure by trampling or as if by trampling

tr: n. 禁忌, 禁止接近, 禁止使用
a. 禁忌的, 忌諱的
vt. 禁忌, 忌諱, 禁止
def: n. a prejudice (especially in Polynesia and other South Pacific islands) that prohibits the use or mention of something because of its sacred nature
n. an inhibition or ban resulting from social custom or emotional aversion
v. declare as sacred and forbidden

ex.en: Discussing salaries remains a taboo in our office.
ex.zh: 在我們辦公室，討論薪資仍是禁忌。

ex.en: Public education can challenge the taboo surrounding mental illness and encourage more people to seek support.
ex.zh: 公眾教育可以挑戰圍繞精神疾病的禁忌，鼓勵更多人尋求支持。

words.tip: 名詞指禁忌；形容詞可說a taboo subject。

tr: n. 討論會, 座談會, 專題報告會, 專題論文集
def: n. a meeting or conference for the public discussion of some topic especially one in which the participants form an audience and make presentations
a meeting where experts discuss a particular subject

ex.en: Leila met several researchers at a symposium yesterday.
ex.zh: 萊拉昨天在一場專題研討會上結識了幾位研究人員。

ex.en: The international symposium brought together scientists to discuss practical solutions to urban air pollution.
ex.zh: 這場國際專題研討會匯聚了科學家，共同討論解決城市空氣汙染的可行辦法。

col: attend a symposium｜參加專題研討會
a symposium on climate change｜氣候變化專題研討會
host a symposium｜主辦專題研討會
words.tip: 複數可用symposia或symposiums。

tr: a. 粗俗的, 庸俗的, 普通的, 通俗的, 方言的
[法] 庸俗的, 卑下的, 粗俗的
def: s lacking refinement or cultivation or taste
s of or associated with the great masses of people
s being or characteristic of or appropriate to everyday language

ex.en: His vulgar joke made everyone at dinner uncomfortable.
ex.zh: 他的粗俗笑話讓餐桌上的每個人都感到不自在。

ex.en: Some viewers argue that vulgar humour on television can encourage disrespectful behaviour among younger audiences.
ex.zh: 一些觀眾認為，電視上的粗俗幽默可能會助長年輕觀眾不尊重他人的行為。

col: vulgar display of wealth｜俗氣的炫富行為
words.tip: 現代常用義帶貶義，不宜用來表示“普通的”。

tr: n. 裂縫, 投幣口, 狹長裂口
vt. 切開, 扯裂, 使有狹縫
def: n. a long narrow opening
n. a narrow fissure
v. make a clean cut through

ex.en: Sunlight came through a narrow slit in the curtains.
ex.zh: 陽光透過窗簾間的一條狹縫照了進來。

ex.en: A narrow slit in the laboratory screen allows researchers to observe how light behaves when passing through small openings.
ex.zh: 實驗室屏障上的一道狹縫讓研究人員能夠觀察光穿過小開口時的表現。

col: slit open an envelope｜裁開信封
a slit in the fabric｜布料上的狹長口子
words.tip: 動詞過去式、過去分詞均為slit；現在分詞為slitting。

def: n. a light fitful sleep

tr: n. 守衛, 門警, 管理人
def: n. someone employed to clean and maintain a building

tr: n. 大臣, 總理, 首相, 大使館/領事館的一等秘書, 司法官, 大學校長
def: n. the person who is head of state (in several countries)
n. the honorary or titular head of a university

tr: n. 核心, 中心, 精髓, 內核
def: n. the inner and usually edible part of a seed or grain or nut or fruit stone
n. a single whole grain of a cereal
n. the choicest or most essential or most vital part of some idea or experience

ex.en: She cracked the walnut and carefully removed the kernel.
ex.zh: 她敲開核桃，小心地取出果仁。

ex.en: Even exaggerated media reports may contain a kernel of truth that deserves further investigation by independent researchers.
ex.zh: 即使是誇大的媒體報道，也可能包含值得獨立研究者進一步調查的些許事實。

col: a kernel of truth｜些許事實
operating system kernel｜操作系統內核
words.tip: kernel指殼內的仁或穀粒，不是桃子等的硬核。

tr: n. 優雅, 風度, 慈悲, 恩惠, 體面, 赦免, 恩典, 謝恩禱告
def: n. (Christian theology) a state of sanctification by God; the state of one who is under such divine influence
n. elegance and beauty of movement or expression
n. a disposition to kindness and compassion

ex.en: The dancer moved across the stage with effortless grace.
ex.zh: 那位舞者輕盈優雅地穿過舞臺。

ex.en: A short grace period can help households manage unexpected delays in receiving their income.
ex.zh: 短暫的寬限期可以幫助家庭應對收入意外延遲到賬的情況。

words.tip: grace 表優雅通常不可數；grace period 指寬限期。

tr: vt. 刺激, 激勵, 引誘
def: v. provoke or stir up
v. to cause to do through pressure or necessity, by physical, moral or intellectual means :"She forced him to take a job in the city"

tr: a. 生動的, 如畫的, 獨特的, 別緻的, 栩栩如生的
def: s. suggesting or suitable for a picture; pretty as a picture
s. strikingly expressive

tr: a. 季度的, 按季度的, 每季的
adv. 按季, 每三個月, 每季一次
def: n. a periodical that is published every quarter (or four issues per year)
a. of or relating to or consisting of a quarter
r. in diagonally opposed quarters of an escutcheon

ex.en: Our club holds quarterly meetings at the local library.
ex.zh: 我們俱樂部每季度在當地的圖書館開一次會。

ex.en: Quarterly reports allow investors to monitor company performance and identify emerging financial risks throughout the year.
ex.zh: 季度報告讓投資者能夠全年跟蹤公司的表現，並識別新出現的財務風險。

words.tip: quarterly指每三個月一次，不是每四個月一次。

tr: vt. 使沮喪, 壓低, 降低, 使蕭條
def: v. lower someone's spirits; make downhearted
v. lower (prices or markets)
v. lessen the activity or force of

ex.en: Days of grey skies and constant rain depress me.
ex.zh: 連日灰暗的天空和不停的雨讓我感到沮喪。

ex.en: High borrowing costs can depress consumer spending, making it harder for small businesses to survive.
ex.zh: 高昂的借貸成本會抑制消費支出，使小企業更難生存。

words.tip: depressed形容人感到沮喪，depressing形容事物令人沮喪。

tr: a. 支流的, 納貢的, 從屬的, 輔助的
n. 支流, 納貢者, 屬國
def: s. (of a stream) flowing into a larger stream
s. paying tribute

tr: n. 地質學, 地質情況
def: n. a science that deals with the history of the earth as recorded in rocks

tr: a. 不尖的, 鈍的, 不得要領的
def: a. not having a point especially a sharp point
Having no useful purpose or chance of achieving anything.

ex.en: It is pointless to water plants during heavy rain.
ex.zh: 下大雨時給植物澆水是徒勞的。

ex.en: Some students consider examinations pointless when they test memorisation rather than practical understanding of a subject.
ex.zh: 當考試考查的是記憶而非對學科的實際理解時，一些學生認為考試毫無意義。

words.tip: 常用 it is pointless to do，表示做某事徒勞。

tr: n. 紗, 紗線, 故事
def: v. tell or spin a yarn
Thread used for knitting or weaving cloth.
An entertaining story, often exaggerated or invented.

ex.en: She chose soft blue yarn for the baby's blanket.
ex.zh: 她挑了柔軟的藍色毛線來織嬰兒毯。

ex.en: Using yarn made from recycled materials can reduce waste in the textile industry.
ex.zh: 使用再生材料製成的紗線可以減少紡織業的廢棄物。

col: a ball of yarn｜一團毛線
words.tip: 作“紗線”通常不可數；作“故事”可數。

tr: n. 懦弱的人, 膽小的人
def: n. a person who shows fear or timidity
n. English dramatist and actor and composer noted for his witty and sophisticated comedies (1899-1973)
Someone who avoids danger or difficulty because of fear

ex.en: He called himself a coward for avoiding the conversation.
ex.zh: 他因為逃避那次談話而罵自己是個懦夫。

ex.en: Calling someone a coward may discourage them from discussing their fears or seeking appropriate support.
ex.zh: 稱某人為膽小鬼，可能會使其不願談論自己的恐懼或尋求適當支持。

col: a complete coward｜十足的膽小鬼
call someone a coward｜稱某人為懦夫
words.tip: coward是名詞，形容詞用cowardly；稱人時含貶義。

def: a. in the same direction as the rotating hands of a clock
r. in the direction that the hands of a clock move
in the same direction as the hands of a clock

ex.en: Turn the lid clockwise until the jar is sealed.
ex.zh: 順時針擰蓋子，直到罐子密封。

ex.en: Visitors move clockwise around the exhibition hall, allowing the museum to manage crowds and prevent congestion.
ex.zh: 參觀者沿順時針方向繞展廳行進，便於博物館管理人流並防止擁堵。

words.tip: 反義詞英式常用anticlockwise，美式常用counterclockwise。

tr: a. 睡眠狀態的, 靜止的
[醫] 休眠的, 不活動的, 休止的
def: s. in a condition of biological rest or suspended animation
a. (of e.g. volcanos) not erupting and not extinct
s. lying with head on paws as if sleeping

ex.en: These plants stay dormant until the weather becomes warmer.
ex.zh: 這些植物會保持休眠狀態，直到天氣轉暖。

ex.en: Although the volcano has remained dormant for centuries, scientists continue to monitor it for signs of renewed activity.
ex.zh: 儘管這座火山已經休眠了數百年，科學家仍持續監測它是否有再次活動的跡象。

col: dormant account｜長期未使用的賬戶
words.tip: 指暫不活動但可能恢復；休眠火山不等於死火山。

def: n. a formal exposition
a long, detailed piece of writing about a particular subject

ex.en: I found a dusty treatise on gardening upstairs.
ex.zh: 我在樓上找到了一本落滿灰塵的園藝專著。

ex.en: The philosopher's treatise on education argues that practical experience should play a central role in learning.
ex.zh: 這位哲學家的教育論著主張，實踐經驗應在學習中發揮核心作用。

words.tip: 常用a treatise on，指系統詳盡的專論而非短文。

tr: n. 淨化, 清除, 瀉藥
v. (使)淨化, 清除, (使)通便
[計] 服務器文件刪除實用程序
def: n. the act of clearing yourself (or another) from some stigma or charge
n. an act of removing by cleansing; ridding of sediment or other undesired elements
n. an abrupt or sudden removal of a person or group from an organization or place

tr: n. 震動, 顫抖, 箭袋
def: n. case for holding arrows
v. shake with fast, tremulous movements
shake slightly with quick, small movements

ex.en: The puppy's legs quivered as it crossed the slippery floor.
ex.zh: 小狗走過溼滑的地板時，雙腿微微發抖。

ex.en: A speaker's voice may quiver under pressure, even when they have prepared thoroughly for a public presentation.
ex.zh: 即使為公開演講做了充分準備，演講者的聲音也可能因壓力而顫抖。

col: a quiver of excitement｜激動得一顫
words.tip: 多指細微而快速的抖動；聲音也可用quiver。

tr: a. 靈敏的, 精巧的, 聰明的
def: s showing inventiveness and skill
Using clever, original ideas to solve problems or make things.

ex.en: He built an ingenious watering system from old bottles.
ex.zh: 他用舊瓶子做了一套巧妙的澆水裝置。

ex.en: Ingenious designs can help architects create comfortable homes on small plots without sacrificing natural light.
ex.zh: 巧妙的設計可以幫助建築師在小塊土地上建造舒適住宅，同時不犧牲自然採光。

col: an ingenious solution｜巧妙的解決辦法
words.tip: 勿混淆：ingenious是巧妙的，ingenuous是天真的。

tr: a. 警覺的, 警戒的, 警惕的
[法] 警醒的, 警戒的, 注意的
def: s carefully observant or attentive; on the lookout for possible danger

tr: vt. 教育, 啟發, 啟蒙, 開導, 教導
def: v. make understand
v. give spiritual insight to; in religion
to give someone information that helps them understand something

ex.en: Could you enlighten me about how this camera works?
ex.zh: 你能給我講講這臺相機怎麼用嗎？

ex.en: Public health campaigns should enlighten citizens about the benefits of vaccination while addressing common concerns respectfully.
ex.zh: 公共衛生宣傳應讓公眾瞭解接種疫苗的益處，同時以尊重的態度回應常見顧慮。

col: an enlightening discussion｜有啟發性的討論
words.tip: 常用enlighten sb about/on sth，語氣較正式。

tr: a. 偶爾發生的, 零星發生的, 分散的
def: a. recurring in scattered and irregular or unpredictable instances

tr: n. 團, 班, 一夥
def: n organization of performers and associated personnel (especially theatrical)
n. a doctor who practices veterinary medicine

tr: n. 尖叫, 倒彩, 強烈抗議, 喊價
def: n a loud utterance; often in protest or opposition
v shout louder than
v utter aloud; often with surprise, horror, or joy

tr: n. 毛孔, 小孔, 氣孔
vi. 專心閱讀, 細想, 鑽研, 沉思, 注視
def: n. any tiny hole admitting passage of a liquid (fluid or gas)
n. any small opening in the skin or outer surface of an animal
a tiny opening in skin or another surface

ex.en: Tiny drops of sweat appeared around his skin pores.
ex.zh: 他的皮膚毛孔周圍冒出了細小的汗珠。

ex.en: Researchers pore over historical records to understand how earlier societies responded to periods of severe drought.
ex.zh: 研究人員仔細研讀歷史記錄，以瞭解過去的社會如何應對嚴重乾旱時期。

col: pore over documents｜仔細研讀文件
words.tip: 動詞常用pore over，勿與pour over混淆。

def: n. an irrational belief arising from ignorance or fear
An unsupported belief linking events or actions to supernatural forces.

ex.en: My uncle avoids walking under ladders because of superstition.
ex.zh: 我叔叔因為迷信，不願從梯子下面走過。

ex.en: Science education can help students distinguish evidence-based explanations from superstition while respecting different cultural traditions.
ex.zh: 科學教育能幫助學生區分有證據支持的解釋與迷信，同時尊重不同的文化傳統。

col: superstition about bad luck｜關於厄運的迷信
words.tip: 泛指迷信用不可數；某種迷信觀念可數。

tr: v. 憤怒地說, 叫嚷, 咆哮
def: n. a dance party that lasts all night and electronically synthesized music is played
n. an extravagantly enthusiastic review
v. participate in an all-night techno dance party

ex.en: My friends keep raving about that little noodle shop.
ex.zh: 我的朋友們一直對那家小麵館讚不絕口。

ex.en: Although critics raved about the exhibition, some visitors questioned whether its high admission price was justified.
ex.zh: 儘管評論家對這場展覽讚不絕口，一些參觀者仍質疑其高昂門票是否合理。

col: rant and rave｜怒氣衝衝地叫嚷
words.tip: rave about 多指讚不絕口，不是對某事咆哮。

tr: n. 怠工, 破壞活動, 破壞
def: n. a deliberate act of destruction or disruption in which equipment is damaged
v. destroy property or hinder normal operations

tr: a. 有償付能力的, 有溶解力的
def: n. a liquid substance capable of dissolving other substances
a. capable of meeting financial obligations
Able to pay all the money that is owed.

ex.en: Careful budgeting kept our small shop solvent this year.
ex.zh: 精打細算使我們的小店今年保持了償債能力。

ex.en: Businesses must remain solvent during economic downturns while continuing to meet their obligations to employees and suppliers.
ex.zh: 經濟低迷期間，企業必須保持償債能力，同時繼續履行對員工和供應商的義務。

col: a solvent company｜有償債能力的公司
words.tip: 形容詞指能償債，不等於盈利；名詞指溶劑。

tr: a. 有責任心的, 負責的, 本著良心的
[法] 憑良心做的, 有道德感的
def: s. characterized by extreme care and great effort
a. guided by or in accordance with conscience or sense of right and wrong
Careful to do duties thoroughly and correctly

ex.en: Our conscientious neighbour checks our plants every morning.
ex.zh: 我們認真負責的鄰居每天早晨都會查看我們的植物。

ex.en: Conscientious employees contribute to workplace safety by following procedures carefully and reporting potential hazards promptly.
ex.zh: 盡責的員工通過認真遵守規程並及時報告潛在危險，為工作場所安全作出貢獻。

col: conscientious about your work｜對工作認真負責
words.tip: conscientious是認真負責的；conscious是有意識的。

def: n. translation of foreign dialogue of a movie or TV program; usually displayed at the bottom of the screen
n. secondary or explanatory title
v. supply (a movie) with subtitles

ex.en: We watched the film with subtitles because the dialogue was quiet.
ex.zh: 因為對白聲音很小，我們看電影時開了字幕。

ex.en: Subtitles can support language learning by helping viewers connect spoken expressions with their written forms.
ex.zh: 字幕能幫助觀眾將口語表達與書面形式聯繫起來，從而輔助語言學習。

words.tip: 影視字幕通常用複數subtitles；單數也可指副標題。

def: v make a tour of a certain place

tr: a. 佔主導地位的, 卓越的
[法] 佔優勢的, 支配其他的, 主要的
def: s most frequent or common
s having superior power and influence

tr: n. 消耗, 耗盡, 放血
[醫] 排除, 缺失(液體), 衰竭[狀態](由於缺液)
def: n. the act of decreasing something markedly
n. the state of being depleted
A reduction in the amount of something available

ex.en: The garden's poor growth suggested depletion of soil nutrients.
ex.zh: 花園裡的植物長勢不佳，說明土壤養分可能已大量流失。

ex.en: Rapid depletion of groundwater threatens agricultural production in regions where rainfall is increasingly unpredictable.
ex.zh: 在降雨越來越難以預測的地區，地下水的快速消耗威脅著農業生產。

words.tip: 常接of，表示資源或儲備減少，不一定已耗盡。

def: n. the act of making a noisy disturbance
Noisy activity and confusion caused by excitement or disturbance

ex.en: A loose puppy caused a commotion in the café.
ex.zh: 一隻沒拴住的小狗在咖啡館裡引起了一陣騷動。

ex.en: The sudden commotion at the station highlighted the need for clearer procedures during unexpected service disruptions.
ex.zh: 車站突發的騷動凸顯了在服務意外中斷時制定更明確應對程序的必要性。

col: a sudden commotion｜突如其來的喧鬧
words.tip: 常指短暫喧鬧或混亂，不一定涉及暴力或暴亂。

tr: n. 禮儀, 禮節, 成規
[法] 規則, 成規, 禮節
def: n. rules governing socially acceptable behavior
Accepted rules of polite behaviour in particular social situations.

ex.en: My aunt taught me basic table etiquette before dinner.
ex.zh: 晚飯前，姑姑教了我基本的餐桌禮儀。

ex.en: Learning local etiquette can help international students avoid misunderstandings and build stronger relationships with their hosts.
ex.zh: 學習當地禮儀可以幫助留學生避免誤會，並與接待他們的人建立更好的關係。

words.tip: 通常不可數；表示禮儀規範，不指單個動作。

tr: n. 怪人, 同性戀者
a. 奇怪的, 不舒服的, 可疑的
def: v. put in a dangerous, disadvantageous, or difficult position
strange or unusual, in an old-fashioned use
describing sexual or gender identities outside heterosexual or conventional categories

ex.en: There was a queer rattling sound inside the cupboard.
ex.zh: 櫥櫃裡傳來一陣奇怪的咔嗒聲。

ex.en: Museums increasingly include queer perspectives to reflect a broader range of experiences in their exhibitions.
ex.zh: 博物館越來越多地納入酷兒視角，以在展覽中呈現更廣泛的人生經歷。

words.tip: “奇怪的”義較舊；身份義宜尊重當事人自稱。

tr: a. 含有...的, 伴著...的, 充滿...的
def: s. marked by distress
s. filled with or attended with

tr: n. 疏忽, 粗心大意, 忽視
def: n. failure to act with the prudence that a reasonable person would exercise under the same circumstances
n. the trait of neglecting responsibilities and lacking concern
Failure to take proper care or fulfil a responsibility

ex.en: The leaking roof resulted from years of negligence.
ex.zh: 屋頂漏水是多年疏於維護造成的。

ex.en: Stronger workplace inspections can help prevent accidents caused by employer negligence and inadequate safety training.
ex.zh: 加強工作場所檢查有助於預防僱主失職及安全培訓不足引發的事故。

words.tip: 不可數名詞，常指未盡應有注意義務的過失。

tr: n. 奔流, 傾盆大雨, 傾注, 迸發
def: n. a violently fast stream of water (or other liquid)

tr: a. 運轉的, 火車頭的, 移動的
def: n. a wheeled vehicle consisting of a self-propelled engine that is used to draw trains along railway tracks
a. of or relating to locomotion
A railway engine that pulls or pushes a train.

ex.en: A steam locomotive pulled the carriages slowly past our platform.
ex.zh: 一臺蒸汽機車拉著車廂，緩緩駛過我們所在的站臺。

ex.en: Replacing diesel locomotives with electric models can reduce local air pollution, especially along busy urban railway routes.
ex.zh: 用電力機車替代柴油機車可以減少當地空氣汙染，尤其是在繁忙的城市鐵路沿線。

words.tip: 指提供動力的機車，不是包含所有車廂的整列火車。

tr: n. 極限, 最大限度, 極度
a. 極度的, 最遠的
def: n. the greatest possible degree
greatest in degree, amount, or intensity
the greatest effort or amount someone can achieve

ex.en: Please handle this delicate glass bowl with utmost care.
ex.zh: 請極其小心地拿放這隻易碎的玻璃碗。

ex.en: Protecting patient privacy is of the utmost importance when hospitals introduce digital systems for storing medical records.
ex.zh: 醫院引入電子病歷存儲系統時，保護患者隱私至關重要。

col: of the utmost importance｜極為重要
words.tip: do one's utmost意為盡最大努力，常接to do。

tr: n. 鬆緊帶, 橡皮筋
a. 有彈性的, 能伸縮的, 可通融的
def: n. a fabric made of yarns containing an elastic material
a. capable of resuming original shape after stretching or compression; springy
s. able to adjust readily to different conditions

ex.en: These elastic sleeves stretch easily over my thick gloves.
ex.zh: 這些有彈性的袖口很容易拉伸，套住我的厚手套。

ex.en: Manufacturers use elastic materials in sports clothing to improve comfort and allow greater freedom of movement.
ex.zh: 製造商在運動服中使用彈性材料，以提高舒適度，讓活動更加自如。

words.tip: 作材料名詞通常不可數；elastic band指橡皮筋。

tr: vt. 困惑, 為難, 使挫折
def: n. a flat plate that controls or directs the flow of fluid or energy
v. check the emission of (sound)
To make someone unable to understand or explain something

ex.en: This puzzle baffled me, so I asked for help.
ex.zh: 這道謎題難倒了我，於是我向別人求助。

ex.en: Unexpected changes in animal migration continue to baffle scientists despite improvements in tracking technology and data collection.
ex.zh: 儘管追蹤技術和數據收集有所改進，動物遷徙中出乎意料的變化仍讓科學家困惑。

col: a baffling mystery｜令人費解的謎團
words.tip: 比confuse更強調完全不理解；常用be baffled by。

tr: vt. 使伸出, 使突出
def: v extend out or project in space
v bulge outward
v swell or protrude outwards

tr: a. 可憐的, 不幸的, 卑鄙的
def: s of very poor quality or condition
s characterized by physical misery
s very unhappy; full of misery

ex.en: I felt wretched after spending the night coughing.
ex.zh: 咳嗽了一整晚後，我感到十分難受。

ex.en: Families living in wretched housing conditions face greater risks of respiratory illness and other health problems.
ex.zh: 居住條件惡劣的家庭面臨更高的呼吸系統疾病及其他健康問題風險。

words.tip: 開頭w不發音；詞尾-ed在此讀/ɪd/。

tr: vt. 將...鑄成合金, 減低成色
def: n. a mixture containing two or more metallic elements or metallic and nonmetallic elements usually fused together or dissolving into each other when molten
v. make an alloy of
A metal made by combining metals or adding other elements.

ex.en: This bicycle frame is made from a lightweight alloy.
ex.zh: 這輛自行車的車架由輕質合金製成。

ex.en: Engineers are developing stronger alloys to reduce vehicle weight and improve fuel efficiency.
ex.zh: 工程師正在開發更堅固的合金，以減輕車輛重量並提高燃油效率。

words.tip: 名詞重音在前；動詞常讀/əˈlɔɪ/。

tr: n. 損害, 傷害, 災禍, 惡作劇, 淘氣
[法] 損害, 傷害, 危害
def: n. reckless or malicious behavior that causes discomfort or annoyance in others
v fall apart
v fold or collapse
v to gather something into small wrinkles or folds

tr: a. 大約的, 接近的, 近似的
vt. 接近, 使接近, 粗略估計
def: v. be close or similar
s. not quite exact or correct
s. very close in resemblance

ex.en: Can you give me an approximate price for the repairs?
ex.zh: 你能告訴我維修大概要多少錢嗎？

ex.en: Researchers used survey responses to calculate the approximate proportion of residents who regularly used public transport.
ex.zh: 研究人員利用調查回復，計算經常使用公共交通的居民所佔的大致比例。

words.tip: 形容詞詞尾讀/mət/，動詞詞尾讀/meɪt/。

def: n. work that a person is expected to do in a specified time
The amount of work someone must complete within a particular period.

ex.en: My workload doubled when two colleagues went on holiday.
ex.zh: 兩位同事休假後，我的工作量增加了一倍。

ex.en: Employers should monitor staff workload carefully to prevent stress and maintain the quality of their services.
ex.zh: 僱主應密切關注員工的工作量，以預防壓力並維持服務質量。

words.tip: 工作量大用heavy workload，而非hard workload。

tr: n. 前奏, 序幕, 序詩, 前奏曲
def: n. music that precedes a fugue or introduces an act in an opera
v. serve as a prelude or opening to
v. play as a prelude

ex.en: Our short walk was a prelude to a lovely picnic.
ex.zh: 我們先散了會兒步，隨後享受了一次愉快的野餐。

ex.en: Investment in reliable internet infrastructure is often a prelude to broader economic development in rural regions.
ex.zh: 投資建設可靠的互聯網基礎設施，往往是農村地區實現更廣泛經濟發展的序幕。

words.tip: 常用a prelude to，to後接名詞或動名詞。

tr: n. 燦爛, 閃爍, 輝耀
vi. 燦爛, 閃爍, 輝耀
def: n. the quality of shining with a bright reflected light
n. the occurrence of a small flash or spark
v. be shiny, as if wet

ex.en: Tiny drops of water glitter on the leaves outside.
ex.zh: 外面樹葉上的小水珠閃閃發亮。

ex.en: Although city skylines glitter at night, excessive artificial lighting can disrupt wildlife and waste energy.
ex.zh: 雖然城市的天際線在夜晚燈光璀璨，但過量的人工照明會干擾野生動物並浪費能源。

col: glitter in the sunlight｜在陽光下閃耀
the glitter of fame｜名聲的耀眼光環
words.tip: 作動詞表示閃耀；作閃光裝飾粉講時通常不可數。

tr: vt. 繁殖, 傳播, 傳送
def: v. transmit from one generation to the next
v. travel through the air
v. transmit

ex.en: Unverified stories propagate quickly when people share them online.
ex.zh: 人們在網上轉發時，未經核實的說法會迅速傳播。

ex.en: Community nurseries can propagate native plants from cuttings, supporting habitat restoration without removing specimens from the wild.
ex.zh: 社區苗圃可以通過扦插繁殖本土植物，支持棲息地修復，而不必從野外移取植株。

col: propagate from cuttings｜通過扦插繁殖
words.tip: 既可指傳播觀念，也可指繁殖植物；語體較正式。

tr: n. 虔誠, 孝敬, 虔誠的行為
def: n. righteousness by virtue of being pious

tr: vt. 使凋謝, 使消亡, 使畏縮
def: v wither, as with a loss of moisture
v lose freshness, vigor, or vitality
To become dry and weak, or cause plants to do so.

ex.en: The flowers withered after a week without water.
ex.zh: 這些花一週沒澆水，都枯萎了。

ex.en: Without sustained investment, local industries may wither, leaving young people with few employment opportunities.
ex.zh: 沒有持續投資，當地產業可能衰退，導致年輕人就業機會寥寥。

col: wither in the heat｜在高溫下枯萎
words.tip: 植物枯萎或事業衰退均可用，常與away連用。

tr: vt. 付還, 償還, 賠償
[經] 償付, 賠還, 付還; 償還
def: v. pay back for some expense incurred

tr: n. 焦油, 柏油, 水手
vt. 塗以焦油, 玷汙, 慫恿
def: v. coat with tar

tr: vt. 熄滅, 使消亡, 壓制, 使減色
def: v. terminate, end, or take out
to stop a fire or flame from burning
to bring a feeling, hope, or idea to an end

ex.en: We extinguished the campfire before getting into our tents.
ex.zh: 我們在進入帳篷前撲滅了篝火。

ex.en: Prolonged unemployment can extinguish young people's hopes of achieving financial independence and securing stable housing.
ex.zh: 長期失業可能使年輕人實現經濟獨立和獲得穩定住房的希望破滅。

words.tip: 及物動詞；日常說撲滅也可用put out。

tr: n. 贖金, 贖身, 贖回
vt. 贖, 贖身, 贖回, 勒索贖金
def: n. money demanded for the return of a captured person
n. payment for the release of someone
n. the act of freeing from captivity or punishment

tr: vt. 開始, 舉行...就職典禮
def: v. commence officially
v. open ceremoniously or dedicate formally
v. be a precursor of

tr: vi. 干預, 撥弄, 賄賂, 損害, 篡改
n. 搗棒, 打夯機, 填塞者
def: v. play around with or alter or falsify, usually secretively or dishonestly

tr: n. 輕蔑, 藐視, 嘲笑, 被嘲弄的人
def: n lack of respect accompanied by a feeling of intense dislike
n open disrespect for a person or thing
v look down on with disdain

tr: n. 背誦, 吟誦, 詳述
[法] 敘述, 評述, 列舉
def: n. performance of music or dance especially by soloists
n. a detailed statement giving facts and figures
n. a detailed account or description of something

ex.en: Her first piano recital drew a small but enthusiastic audience.
ex.zh: 她的首場鋼琴獨奏會吸引了人數不多卻十分熱情的觀眾。

ex.en: Regular opportunities to give a recital can help music students develop confidence and improve their performance skills.
ex.zh: 定期舉辦獨奏會的機會可以幫助音樂專業學生建立信心並提高演奏技巧。

col: a recital of facts｜事實的逐一陳述
words.tip: 音樂語境多指獨奏或獨唱，不等於大型演唱會。

tr: n. 轉向, 彎曲, 背離
vi. 突然轉向, 轉彎, 背離
vt. 使突然轉向, 使轉彎, 使背離
def: n. the act of turning aside suddenly
v. turn sharply; change direction abruptly
To change direction suddenly, especially to avoid hitting something.

ex.en: The cyclist swerved to avoid a branch on the road.
ex.zh: 騎車人突然轉向，避開了路上的樹枝。

ex.en: Poorly maintained roads may force drivers to swerve unexpectedly, increasing the risk of collisions with other vehicles.
ex.zh: 養護不善的道路可能迫使司機突然轉向，增加與其他車輛相撞的風險。

col: swerve to avoid something｜突然轉向避開某物
swerve off the road｜突然偏離道路
words.tip: 強調突然改變方向；普通轉彎通常用turn。

tr: v. 毀壞, 破壞, 掠奪
def: n. (usually plural) a destructive action

tr: a. 潛伏性的, 隱藏的
def: s. potentially existing but not presently evident or realized
s. (pathology) not presently active
Present but not yet active, visible, or fully developed.

ex.en: Her first pottery class revealed a latent artistic talent.
ex.zh: 第一堂陶藝課顯露了她潛在的藝術天賦。

ex.en: Supportive teaching can help students develop latent abilities that conventional examinations may fail to identify.
ex.zh: 支持性的教學能幫助學生髮展傳統考試可能無法識別的潛在能力。

words.tip: 指已經存在但尚未顯現或發揮作用。

def: s. crushed by grief
Empty of people and lacking signs of life
Feeling completely alone and deeply unhappy

ex.en: We crossed a desolate valley before reaching the village.
ex.zh: 我們穿過一片荒涼的山谷，才到達村莊。

ex.en: Former industrial sites often remain desolate until public investment brings new housing and green spaces.
ex.zh: 昔日的工業用地往往一直荒涼，直到公共投資帶來新住房和綠地。

col: a desolate village｜荒無人煙的村莊
words.tip: 形容地方指荒涼，形容人則指孤獨淒涼。

tr: vt. 弄亂, 使混亂, 使脫去衣服
n. 無秩序, 雜亂, 不整齊的衣著
def: n. untidiness (especially of clothing and appearance)
A state of disorder or lack of organisation.

ex.en: The kitchen was in disarray after our baking afternoon.
ex.zh: 我們做了一下午烘焙後，廚房一片狼藉。

ex.en: Without clear leadership, emergency planning can fall into disarray, leaving communities poorly prepared for extreme weather.
ex.zh: 缺乏明確的領導，應急規劃就可能陷入混亂，導致社區無法充分應對極端天氣。

words.tip: 常作不可數名詞，常用in disarray表示處於混亂。

tr: n. 使人痛苦的東西, 折磨者, 苦痛
vt. 使苦惱, 糾纏, 歪曲, 拷問
def: v. torment emotionally or mentally
v. treat cruelly
severe physical pain or mental suffering

ex.en: The constant itching was a torment all night.
ex.zh: 持續的瘙癢折磨了我整整一夜。

ex.en: Persistent uncertainty about employment can torment workers and undermine their mental health over time.
ex.zh: 就業狀況長期不確定會折磨勞動者，並逐漸損害他們的心理健康。

words.tip: 名詞重音在首音節；動詞重音在第二音節。

tr: vt. 誤用, 濫用, 虐待
def: n. improper or excessive use
To use something incorrectly or for a harmful purpose.
The incorrect or harmful use of something.

ex.en: You could damage that knife if you misuse it.
ex.zh: 如果使用不當，你可能會弄壞那把刀。

ex.en: Organisations that misuse personal data risk losing public trust and may face substantial legal penalties.
ex.zh: 濫用個人數據的機構可能失去公眾信任，並面臨嚴厲的法律處罰。

col: misuse personal data｜濫用個人數據
misuse of resources｜資源的不當使用
words.tip: 動詞詞尾讀/ z /，名詞詞尾讀/ s /。

tr: vt. 瀰漫於, 遍及於, 流行於, 蔓延, 滲透於, 充滿
def: v spread or diffuse through
to spread throughout a place or affect every part

ex.en: The smell of fresh bread pervaded the kitchen.
ex.zh: 新鮮麵包的香味瀰漫了整個廚房。

ex.en: Digital technology now pervades everyday life, changing how people communicate, study, and access public services.
ex.zh: 數字技術如今滲透日常生活，改變著人們交流、學習和獲取公共服務的方式。

col: pervade the atmosphere｜瀰漫在氣氛中
a sense of unease pervades｜不安感瀰漫
words.tip: 及物動詞，直接接場所或領域，不加介詞。

tr: a. 可以忽略的, 不足取的, 無用的
[醫] 可不計的, 可忽視的
def: s. so small as to be meaningless; insignificant
s. not worth considering

tr: n. 懸疑, 焦慮, 懸念, 懸而不決
def: n. apprehension about what is going to happen
n. an uncertain cognitive state
n. excited anticipation of an approaching climax

tr: n. 施捨物, 救濟品, 分發的印刷品資料, 廣告物品
def: n. an announcement distributed to members of the press in order to supplement or replace an oral presentation
n. giving money or food or clothing to a needy person
A document given to people attending a lesson or meeting.

ex.en: Our teacher gave us a handout about healthy eating.
ex.zh: 老師給我們發了一份關於健康飲食的講義。

ex.en: A well-designed handout can help students review key concepts independently after a lecture has finished.
ex.zh: 一份設計得當的講義可以幫助學生在講座結束後獨立複習核心概念。

words.tip: handout是名詞；hand out是動詞短語，意為分發。

tr: a. 微弱的, 衰弱的, 無效的
def: s. pathetically lacking in force or effectiveness
s. lacking strength
Lacking physical strength, energy, or intensity.

ex.en: After the illness, he felt too feeble to cook.
ex.zh: 病後他感到很虛弱，連飯都做不了。

ex.en: Feeble enforcement of environmental regulations allows some factories to continue polluting rivers without facing meaningful consequences.
ex.zh: 環境法規執行不力，使一些工廠得以繼續汙染河流，而不必承擔實質性後果。

col: a feeble excuse｜站不住腳的藉口
words.tip: 可形容身體、聲音，也可批評藉口或努力無力。

tr: n. 補藥, (音樂)主調音或基音
a. 滋補的, 聲調的, 使精神振作的
def: n. lime- or lemon-flavored carbonated water containing quinine
n. (music) the first note of a diatonic scale
n. a medicine that strengthens and invigorates

ex.en: The pharmacist suggested a tonic for my persistent tiredness.
ex.zh: 藥劑師建議我服用一種補劑來緩解持續的疲倦。

ex.en: Regular access to green spaces can act as a tonic for residents facing the pressures of urban life.
ex.zh: 經常接觸綠地能讓承受城市生活壓力的居民感到振奮。

col: a tonic for the mind｜振奮精神的事物
words.tip: 比喻用法常見a tonic for，指讓人振奮的事物。

tr: n. 貴族, 高尚, 貴族階級
def: n. a privileged class holding hereditary titles
n. the quality of elevation of mind and exaltation of character or ideals or conduct
n. the state of being of noble birth
n. a hole made by an animal, usually for shelter
v. move through by or as by digging
A hole or tunnel dug by an animal for shelter

ex.en: A rabbit disappeared into its burrow beneath the hedge.
ex.zh: 一隻兔子鑽進樹籬下的地洞，不見了。

ex.en: Animals that burrow underground can improve soil quality by allowing air and water to penetrate deeper layers.
ex.zh: 在地下挖洞的動物能讓空氣和水進入更深的土層，從而改善土壤質量。

col: burrow into the ground｜鑽入地下
burrow under a blanket｜鑽到毯子下面
words.tip: burrow指挖洞或地洞；別與borrow（借入）混淆。

tr: n. 行為不良, 失職
[經] 毀約, 怠工, 曠職
def: n. nonpayment of a debt when due
n. a tendency to be negligent and uncaring
n. an antisocial misdeed in violation of the law by a minor

ex.en: Our youth club helps teenagers stay away from delinquency.
ex.zh: 我們的青少年俱樂部幫助青少年遠離違法行為。

ex.en: Affordable recreational facilities and supportive mentoring programmes may help reduce juvenile delinquency in disadvantaged neighbourhoods.
ex.zh: 價格可負擔的娛樂設施和支持性的輔導項目可能有助於減少弱勢社區的青少年違法行為。

words.tip: 常見於juvenile delinquency，不能泛指普通小錯誤。

tr: n. 電車, 手推車, 臺車
def: n a wheeled vehicle that runs on rails and is propelled by electricity
A wheeled cart used for carrying shopping or other items.
An electric passenger vehicle that runs on rails in streets.

ex.en: She pushed a trolley full of groceries towards the checkout.
ex.zh: 她推著裝滿食品雜貨的購物車走向收銀臺。

ex.en: Airports should provide free luggage trolleys to make travelling easier for families and older passengers.
ex.zh: 機場應提供免費行李車，方便家庭和老年乘客出行。

words.tip: 英式購物車用trolley，美式通常用shopping cart。

def: n warm-blooded egg-laying vertebrates characterized by feathers and forelimbs modified as wings
n the flesh of a bird or fowl (wild or domestic) used as food
n informal terms for a (young) woman

tr: a. 臉上發紅, 發熱的, 潮熱的, 肺病的
n. 臉紅, 潮熱病人
def: s marked by intense agitation or emotion
extremely busy and full of activity, often causing stress

ex.en: After a hectic morning, I finally sat down for lunch.
ex.zh: 忙亂了一上午後，我終於坐下來吃午飯。

ex.en: A hectic urban lifestyle can leave residents with little time for exercise, relaxation, or meaningful social interaction.
ex.zh: 忙碌緊張的城市生活可能讓居民無暇鍛鍊、放鬆或進行有意義的社交。

col: a hectic schedule｜緊湊忙碌的日程
a hectic lifestyle｜忙碌緊張的生活方式
words.tip: 現代常用義是忙亂的，不是興奮的或發熱的。

tr: a. 不流動的, 停滯的, 不景氣的, 蕭條的, 汙濁的, 遲鈍的
def: s. not growing or changing; without force or vitality

tr: a. 遷移的, 流浪的
def: a. used of animals that move seasonally
Moving between regions regularly, often with the seasons.

ex.en: Migratory birds gather by the lake every spring.
ex.zh: 每年春天，候鳥都會聚集在湖邊。

ex.en: Protecting wetlands along migratory routes is essential because many bird species depend on these habitats for food and rest.
ex.zh: 保護遷徙路線沿途的溼地至關重要，因為許多鳥類依靠這些棲息地覓食和休息。

words.tip: 常形容鳥類等季節性遷徙，不等於漫無目的流浪。

tr: vt. 統治, 威壓, 打敗, 駁回
[法] 否決, 駁回, 批駁
def: v. rule against
To use authority to reject or reverse a decision or objection.

ex.en: The manager overruled my request to close the shop early.
ex.zh: 經理否決了我提前關店的請求。

ex.en: National authorities may overrule local planning decisions when major infrastructure projects serve the wider public interest.
ex.zh: 當重大基礎設施項目符合更廣泛的公共利益時，國家主管部門可能否決地方規劃決定。

words.tip: 強調憑更高權力否決，不只是表示不同意。

tr: vi. 從屬於, 關於, 涉及, 附屬, 適合, 相稱
[法] 屬於, 從屬, 附屬
def: v. be a part or attribute of
To relate to or apply to a particular subject.

ex.en: These rules pertain to everyone who uses the kitchen.
ex.zh: 這些規定適用於所有使用廚房的人。

ex.en: The committee reviewed documents pertaining to water quality before recommending stricter controls on industrial waste.
ex.zh: 委員會在建議加強工業廢物管控之前，審閱了有關水質的文件。

words.tip: 正式用語，通常接to；常見結構為pertaining to。

tr: a. 無疑的, 確定的
adv. 無疑地, 確定地
def: r without doubt; certainly
Almost certainly, or as one confidently expects.

ex.en: You'll doubtless feel hungry after such a long walk.
ex.zh: 走了這麼遠，你想必餓了。

ex.en: Improved public transport will doubtless benefit commuters, although its construction may cause temporary disruption.
ex.zh: 改善公共交通想必會使通勤者受益，不過施工可能造成暫時的不便。

words.tip: 常表示有把握的推測，不一定是絕對確定。

tr: a. 笨重的, 麻煩的, 累贅的
def: s. difficult to handle or use especially because of size or weight

tr: a. 間歇的, 斷斷續續的
def: s. stopping and starting at irregular intervals
Stopping and starting repeatedly rather than continuing without a break.

ex.en: Intermittent rain kept us running indoors throughout the afternoon.
ex.zh: 整個下午，斷斷續續的雨讓我們不時跑回屋裡。

ex.en: Intermittent internet access can prevent rural students from participating fully in online learning programmes.
ex.zh: 網絡連接時斷時續，會妨礙農村學生充分參與在線學習課程。

words.tip: 強調時停時續，不一定按固定週期發生。

tr: a. 目不識丁的, 沒受教育的
def: n. a person unable to read
a. not able to read or write
a. lacking culture, especially in language and literature

ex.en: Her grandfather was illiterate but told wonderful bedtime stories.
ex.zh: 她的祖父雖然不識字，卻很會講睡前故事。

ex.en: Free adult education can help illiterate citizens develop essential skills and participate more fully in society.
ex.zh: 免費的成人教育能夠幫助不識字的公民掌握基本技能，更充分地參與社會生活。

words.tip: 名詞用法易顯貶義，宜用形容詞客觀描述。

tr: n. 特權, 君權, 職權
a. 特權的, 行使特權的
def: n. a right reserved exclusively by a particular person or group (especially a hereditary or official right)
a special right belonging to a particular person or group

ex.en: Choosing the final design is the team leader's prerogative.
ex.zh: 選定最終設計方案是組長的專有權利。

ex.en: Decisions about public spending should not be the exclusive prerogative of a small group of officials.
ex.zh: 公共支出的決策不應成為少數官員獨享的特權。

words.tip: 指特定身份享有的權利，不是人人都有的普通權利。

tr: vt. 刻上, 雕刻, 銘記
def: v. impress or affect deeply
v. carve or cut into a block used for printing or print from such a block
v. carve or cut a design or letters into

tr: a. 有惡意的, 惡性的, 有害的
def: a. dangerous to health; characterized by progressive and uncontrolled growth (especially of a tumor)

tr: n. 團體, 協會, 行業協會
def: n a formal association of people with similar interests

tr: vt. 逐出, 趕出, 驅逐
[法] 逐出, 驅逐, 沒收
def: v. expel or eject without recourse to legal process
v. expel from one's property or force to move out by a legal process
To legally force someone to leave a property

ex.en: The landlord threatened to evict us over unpaid rent.
ex.zh: 房東威脅要因我們拖欠房租而將我們趕走。

ex.en: Stronger tenant protections could prevent landlords from evicting vulnerable families without adequate notice or legal justification.
ex.zh: 加強租戶保護，可以防止房東在未充分提前通知或缺乏法律依據的情況下驅逐弱勢家庭。

col: evict someone from a property｜將某人逐出房產
words.tip: 常用evict somebody from；尤其指依法逐出租屋。

def: n. the manner in which something is expressed in words
The particular words chosen to express something.

ex.en: The wording of your message sounds a little formal.
ex.zh: 你這條消息的措辭聽起來有點正式。

ex.en: Careful wording in public health announcements can prevent confusion and encourage people to follow advice.
ex.zh: 公共衛生公告採用嚴謹的措辭，可以避免誤解並鼓勵人們遵循建議。

words.tip: 通常不可數；強調具體措辭，不是籠統的語言。

tr: vt. 搶劫, 劫持, 敲詐
[法] 擋路搶劫, 搶劫, 綁架
def: n. seizure of a vehicle in transit either to rob it or divert it to an alternate destination
v. seize control of
to illegally seize control of a vehicle during a journey

ex.en: One guest hijacked the conversation to discuss his own problems.
ex.zh: 一位客人把話題全轉到了自己的煩惱上。

ex.en: Powerful interest groups may hijack public debates, preventing communities from discussing their most urgent concerns.
ex.zh: 強勢利益集團可能操控公共討論，使社區無法討論自身最迫切的問題。

col: hijack the conversation｜把談話據為己用
words.tip: 本義是劫持交通工具；也可比喻操控討論或議程。

tr: a. 散開的, 瀰漫的
def: v. move outward
s. spread out; not concentrated in one place
s. lacking conciseness

ex.en: The scent of fresh bread diffused through the kitchen.
ex.zh: 新鮮麵包的香味在廚房裡瀰漫開來。

ex.en: Public libraries help diffuse knowledge throughout society by providing free access to reliable information and educational resources.
ex.zh: 公共圖書館通過免費提供可靠信息和教育資源，幫助知識在全社會傳播。

words.tip: 動詞詞尾讀/z/，形容詞讀/s/；勿混defuse（化解）。

tr: a. 繁茂的, 豐富的, 生氣勃勃的
[醫] 生成過多的, 高度增生的
興高采烈的；熱情洋溢的
def: s. produced or growing in extreme abundance
full of energy, excitement, and happiness
growing abundantly or richly decorated and imaginative

ex.en: The exuberant puppy bounced around the garden all morning.
ex.zh: 那隻活力十足的小狗整個上午都在花園裡蹦來蹦去。

ex.en: Exuberant celebrations at international sporting events can create a powerful sense of shared identity among spectators.
ex.zh: 國際體育賽事中熱情洋溢的慶祝活動能讓觀眾產生強烈的共同認同感。

col: an exuberant personality｜熱情奔放的性格
words.tip: 核心是活力或豐富程度高，不等於“華而不實”。

tr: a. 分離的, 被隔離的
vi. 分離, 隔離, 分凝
vt. 使分離, 使隔離
def: n. someone who is or has been segregated
v. separate by race or religion; practice a policy of racial segregation
v. divide from the main body or mass and collect

ex.en: The club refused to segregate children by family income.
ex.zh: 這傢俱樂部拒絕按家庭收入將孩子分開。

ex.en: Schools that segregate pupils by social background may reinforce inequality rather than promote mutual understanding.
ex.zh: 按社會背景隔離學生的學校可能會加劇不平等，而非促進相互理解。

col: racially segregated schools｜實行種族隔離的學校
words.tip: segregate A from B指把A與B隔離。

tr: vt. 想, 考慮, 計劃
def: v reflect deeply on a subject
v think intently and at length, as for spiritual purposes
to focus your mind calmly, often as a mental exercise

ex.en: I meditate for ten minutes before breakfast each morning.
ex.zh: 我每天早飯前都會冥想十分鐘。

ex.en: Some employers encourage staff to meditate during breaks as a way of managing workplace stress.
ex.zh: 一些僱主鼓勵員工在休息時冥想，以緩解工作壓力。

col: meditate on something｜深入思考某事
words.tip: 表示深思某事，常用meditate on或upon。

tr: a. 品德高尚的, 公正的, 貞潔的, 有效力的
def: a. morally excellent

tr: vi. 流產, 中途失敗
vt. 使流產, 使失敗, 使中止
def: n. the act of terminating a project or procedure before it is completed
v. terminate before completion
v. cease development, die, and be aborted

tr: vt. 調合, 捏造, 編造
def: v. make a concoction (of) by mixing
v. prepare or cook by mixing ingredients

tr: n. 狂躁, 熱衷, 狂熱
def: n. an irrational but irresistible motive for a belief or action
n. a mood disorder; an affective disorder in which the victim tends to respond excessively and sometimes violently
an unusually strong enthusiasm for an activity or object

ex.en: A mania for collecting toy trains swept our neighbourhood.
ex.zh: 收集玩具火車的熱潮席捲了我們社區。

ex.en: During episodes of mania, individuals may need professional support to manage sleep disruption and impulsive behaviour.
ex.zh: 在躁狂發作期間，患者可能需要專業支持來應對睡眠紊亂和衝動行為。

col: an episode of mania｜一次躁狂發作
words.tip: 日常可指狂熱；醫學上的躁狂不等於普通興奮。

def: n. brightness enough to blind partially and temporarily
v. to cause someone to lose clear vision, especially from intense light
v. amaze or bewilder, as with brilliant wit or intellect or skill

tr: n. 喝彩, 歡呼, 贊同
v. 歡呼, 喝彩, 稱讚
def: n. enthusiastic approval
v. praise vociferously
strong public praise for someone or something

ex.en: Her first film won acclaim at the local festival.
ex.zh: 她的首部電影在當地電影節上贏得了讚譽。

ex.en: The new public library has received widespread acclaim for its accessible design and sustainable construction.
ex.zh: 這座新公共圖書館因其無障礙設計和可持續建築方式而廣受讚譽。

words.tip: 名詞通常不可數；動詞常用be acclaimed as被譽為。

tr: n. 觸鬚, 觸手, 觸角
def: n. something that acts like a tentacle in its ability to grasp and hold
n. any of various elongated tactile or prehensile flexible organs that occur on the head or near the mouth in many animals; used for feeling or grasping or locomotion
a long flexible animal part used for touching or grasping

ex.en: The octopus wrapped a tentacle around a small shell.
ex.zh: 章魚用一條觸手纏住了一枚小貝殼。

ex.en: Each tentacle helps the octopus explore its surroundings and capture food in complex marine habitats.
ex.zh: 每條觸手都幫助章魚探索周圍環境，並在複雜的海洋棲息地中捕食。

words.tip: 章魚、水母的觸手用tentacle；昆蟲觸角用antenna。

tr: a. 費力的, 努力的, 險峻的
def: s. characterized by effort to the point of exhaustion; especially physical effort
s. taxing to the utmost; testing powers of endurance
s. difficult to accomplish; demanding considerable mental effort and skill

ex.en: The arduous climb left us exhausted but deeply satisfied.
ex.zh: 這段艱苦的攀登讓我們筋疲力盡，卻也十分滿足。

ex.en: Restoring damaged ecosystems is an arduous process that requires sustained investment and cooperation between scientists and local communities.
ex.zh: 修復受損生態系統是一個艱鉅的過程，需要持續投資以及科學家與當地社區的合作。

words.tip: 強調長期費力，常修飾task、journey、process。

tr: a. 溫和的, 適度的, 有節制的, 溫帶的
def: a. (of weather or climate) free from extremes; mild; or characteristic of such weather or climate
a. not extreme in behavior
Having weather that is neither very hot nor very cold

ex.en: We enjoy walking outdoors in this temperate climate.
ex.zh: 這裡氣候溫和，我們喜歡在戶外散步。

ex.en: Temperate regions may experience significant changes in rainfall patterns as global temperatures continue to rise.
ex.zh: 隨著全球氣溫持續上升，溫帶地區的降雨模式可能發生顯著變化。

words.tip: 氣候義指不太冷也不太熱；不等於熱帶的。

tr: n. 資質, 才能, 自然傾向
def: n. inherent ability
A natural ability to learn or do something well

ex.en: Leila showed an aptitude for music at school.
ex.zh: 萊拉在學校裡展現出了音樂天賦。

ex.en: Schools should recognise practical aptitude as well as academic achievement when advising students about careers.
ex.zh: 學校在為學生提供職業建議時，既應重視學業成績，也應認可實踐方面的天賦。

col: an aptitude for languages｜語言天賦
show an aptitude for｜展現出某方面的天賦
words.tip: 常用aptitude for，後接名詞或動名詞。

def: n. a state in northwestern North America; the 49th state admitted to the union
v. make laws, bills, etc. or bring into effect by legislation
n. the act of pouncing
v. move down on as if in an attack
To jump suddenly towards something to catch or attack it.

ex.en: Our kitten pounced on a leaf blowing across the garden.
ex.zh: 我們的小貓猛撲向一片被風吹過花園的葉子。

ex.en: News outlets often pounce on minor errors, distracting audiences from more important policy debates.
ex.zh: 新聞媒體常常抓住小錯誤不放，使受眾忽略更重要的政策討論。

col: pounce on an opportunity｜立即抓住機會
pounce on a mistake｜揪住錯誤不放
words.tip: 常接on，既可指猛撲，也可指抓住機會或錯誤。

tr: n. 一絲光線, 微光, 少許
def: n a flash of light (especially reflected light)
n a slight suggestion or vague understanding
v shine brightly, like a star or a light

ex.en: A glimmer of candlelight escaped through the closed curtains.
ex.zh: 一縷燭光從拉攏的窗簾縫隙中透出來。

ex.en: Recent improvements in water quality offer a glimmer of hope for communities affected by industrial pollution.
ex.zh: 近期水質的改善為受工業汙染影響的社區帶來了一線希望。

col: a glimmer of light｜一縷微光
a glimmer of hope｜一線希望
a glimmer of understanding｜一絲領悟
words.tip: a glimmer of hope是“一線希望”的常見表達。

tr: n. 災難, 不幸事件
def: n. an event resulting in great loss and misfortune
An event causing severe damage, suffering, or distress.

ex.en: The flood was a calamity for the whole village.
ex.zh: 這場洪水給整個村莊帶來了災難。

ex.en: Effective emergency planning can reduce the human and economic costs of a natural calamity.
ex.zh: 有效的應急規劃可以減少自然災難造成的人員損失和經濟代價。

words.tip: 比problem嚴重得多，常指造成重大損失的災難。

tr: a. 平靜的, 溫和的, 沉著的, 平穩的
